item.content:encoded:
News / Cointelegraph / Bitcoin price ignores Anthropic debut as ANT share price dips below $100

Bitcoin price ignores Anthropic debut as ANT share price dips below $100 1 min read

BTCUSD ANT Bitcoin shrugged off US tech-stock strength at Thursday’s Wall Street open as markets reacted to Anthropic’s $111.50 debut. Key points: Anthropic opens at $111.50 per share on the Nasdaq, 34% above its IPO price of $83, rising as high as $115 before dropping to lows of $95.05. Bitcoin (BTC) struggled to follow equities’ upside as sell-side pressure kept BTCUSD near four-month lows of $62,000. Anthropic debut sees share price near 40% gain versus IPO Data from TradingView showed BTCUSD falling to $62,250 as US stock markets headed higher.

BTCUSD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView Excitement around Anthropic initially fueled 0.6% daily gains for the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index, which subsequently turned red on the day, down 1% at the time of writing. That followed 1.4% daily upside for South Korea’s tech-focused KOSPI Composite Index.

Nasdaq Composite Index one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView Trading of the company’s stock on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT began at $111.50, 34% above its IPO price of $83, reaching a local high of $115 before dropping below the $100 mark amid ongoing volatility.

Anthropic shares one-minute chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView Perpetual futures traders on Hyperliquid had already placed fair value at around $103, based on a company valuation of around $1.845 trillion. Reacting, trading resource The Kobeissi Letter noted that the opening had pushed the valuation above $2 trillion, putting it in sixth place among the world’s most valuable public companies. Previously, Cointelegraph reported on the record-breaking IPO helping to renew market trust in the AI sector amid ongoing uncertainty over Nvidia following the ousting of its CEO Jensen Huang. “With some of the tumultuous times here for Nvidia, a little bit of that trust has gone away from the retail investor so this is the way people I think are going to express themselves,” J.J. Kinahan, senior vice president of retail and alternative investments at CBOE Global Markets, told CNBC. In his latest analysis, economist Mohamed El-Erian called the IPO “historic.” “On the micro side: In five years, it has gone from a startup to one of the world’s most valuable companies. It’s the largest IPO ever. On the macro side: Lots worth monitoring, starting with the flow-of-funds implications,” he summarized.

item.content:encoded:
News / GuruFocus / Nvidia Stocks Rise 4.63% as $10 Billion Anthropic Stake Lands on IPO Day

Nvidia Stocks Rise 4.63% as $10 Billion Anthropic Stake Lands on IPO Day Less than 1 min read

NVDA ANT Nvidia NVDA shares rose 4.63% to $157.95 at 9:45 a.m. ET on November 19 in regular trading, as Anthropic's final prospectus confirmed that Nvidia will buy 120,481,927 Class N shares for about $10.0 billion at the $83 IPO price. The bounce follows a rough week. Shares had dropped more than 13% over the past week after Jensen Huang's resignation, and new chair Harvey Jones said on the earnings call that the board does not intend to reinstate him. The operating engine is not the problem. Third-quarter revenue reached $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier, with a 74.8% GAAP gross margin and $2.70 of diluted EPS. Guidance calls for $130.0 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, plus or minus 3%, with no China data center compute revenue assumed. Nvidia returned $28.1 billion to shareholders in the quarter and still has about $227.3 billion left on its buyback authorization.

The $10 billion Anthropic cheque equals roughly 15% of last quarter's $65.3 billion net income, a manageable bet that also deepens ties with a key GPU customer. The GuruFocus page shows a GF Score of 91/100, built on near-perfect profitability and a fortress balance sheet. Yet the share price sits about 62% below the GF Value of $418.87, and GuruFocus flags a possible value trap. That gap suggests the market is pricing governance and China risk, not earnings. The next test is Huang's Capitol Hill appearances in December and whether hyperscaler orders hold under interim leadership.

item.content:encoded:
News / GuruFocus / Broadcom Stocks Rise 4.21% as Chip Supplier Joins Anthropic's $26 Billion Placement

Broadcom Stocks Rise 4.21% as Chip Supplier Joins Anthropic's $26 Billion Placement Less than 1 min read

AVGO Broadcom AVGO shares rose 4.21% to $368.96 at 9:45 a.m. ET on November 19 in regular trading, after Anthropic's final prospectus listed Broadcom among seven strategic buyers in a $26.0 billion private placement at the $83 IPO price. Broadcom will take 12,048,192 Class N shares for about $1.0 billion. The filing describes Broadcom as both a supplier and a lessor to Anthropic, which runs a multi-chip setup across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, Nvidia GPUs and AMD GPUs. Anthropic disclosed about $900.9 billion of aggregate committed spend on purchase commitments and leases, substantially all tied to compute. CNBC noted chipmakers broadly advanced before the listing.

A $1 billion stake is under 0.1% of Broadcom's $1.76 trillion market value, so the equity is a signal, not a profit driver. The real exposure is custom silicon and networking inside that $900.9 billion pipeline. GuruFocus rates Broadcom 98/100, with top profitability and strong value and growth readings. Shares trade about 19% below the GF Value of $454.06, which GuruFocus labels modestly undervalued. Broadcom's next quarterly report and its AI semiconductor revenue guidance will be the clearest read on that pipeline.
